_comment: THE LAST CUSTOMER (GDD 26). Written 2026-08-12; NOT LOADED YET — the parser lands in PLAN_last_call S1/S5. Everything here is real data against the real catalogue: every 'recipe' is an id from recipes.json, every 'look' is a slug the cast already has a face for, and every 'needStyle' is a style the market actually sells. Names and lines are the author's to replace; the SHAPE is the design (GDD 26 sections 4, 5 and 7): the ask names what is missing, no beat is a dead end, two lines a beat and one sentence each.

characters.name: Graham Sedgwick
characters.blurb: Collects for the building. Never raises his voice, never has to.

characters.name: Meredith Nolan
characters.blurb: Drank here before it was yours. Knows which stool was whose.

characters.name: Ulrich Brenner
characters.blurb: Writes about rooms like this one. Orders the same drink everywhere, on purpose.

ask: So you are the one who took it on.
A whiskey. Neat. I will wait while you look.
nudge: Still nothing brown on that shelf.
servedRight: The building can wait a week. Do not make me come back twice.
servedWrong: That is not whiskey, and we both know it.
declined: Then buy a bottle. I will come back.

ask: He used to make me a mule when the room got loud.
Ginger, lime, the copper cup he never actually owned.
nudge: No ginger yet. He always said it was the cheap half.
servedRight: Close enough that I had to put it down for a second.
Keep the recipe. It was his.
declined: It is a small thing to stock. I will ask again.

ask: A Manhattan. Stirred — I will know the difference.
Here is how it is built. Every room gets one honest paragraph; this is yours.
nudge: Vermouth. It is not an optional ingredient, it is half the drink.
servedRight: Stirred, cold, and not drowned. Good.
I will say the room is worth the walk.
servedWrong: You shook it. I can see the ice in it from here.
declined: An honest no is worth a paragraph too. Later, then.
